examples.ko: 아이가 콜록 기침을 하더니 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: The child coughed and then drank some water.

examples.ko: 옆 사람이 콜록 하고 기침을 했어요.
examples.en: The person next to me gave a cough.

examples.ko: 밤새 콜록 소리가 들려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I heard coughing all night and couldn't sleep.
Grandfather came out of the room with a cough.

examples.ko: 먼지가 많아서 저도 모르게 콜록 기침이 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was so much dust that I coughed without meaning to.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 콜록 하고 기침이 나와서 민망했어요.
examples.en: I coughed during the meeting and felt embarrassed.

explain: 기침 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 한 번만 할 때는 '콜록', 여러 번 계속할 때는 '콜록콜록'이라고 많이 말해요. 재채기 소리는 '에취'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: This imitates the sound of a cough. People say '콜록' for one cough and '콜록콜록' when it keeps going. A sneeze sounds like '에취', which is different.

examples.en: I've been coughing all day because of my cold.
If you keep coughing, please go see a doctor.
The person next to me kept coughing, so I was worried.
Why are you coughing so much since this morning?
I could hear the child coughing all night.
Many people are wearing masks and coughing.

explain: '기침하다'는 그냥 기침을 한다는 말이고, '콜록거리다'는 기침 소리가 계속 나는 모습을 생생하게 말할 때 써요. 주로 감기에 걸렸을 때 들어요. '콜록거리다' 말고 '콜록콜록하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '기침하다' simply says someone coughs, while '콜록거리다' vividly describes the sound of repeated coughing. It is mostly used when someone has a cold. People also say '콜록콜록하다'.

examples.en: The sides of my nose turned red from the cold.
When he gets angry, his nostrils flare.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 콧방울 주변을 꼼꼼히 발라요.
examples.en: When I put on makeup, I carefully cover the area around the sides of my nose.
There is a small mole on the side of my nose.
The baby twitches its nostrils while sleeping.
My skin was dry even on the sides of my nose, so I put on cream.

explain: 코끝보다 아래쪽 옆, 콧구멍 둘레의 동그란 부분을 말해요. '콧방울이 벌렁거리다'처럼 화나거나 숨이 찰 때의 모습에 자주 써요. 화장이나 피부 관리 이야기에서도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: This is the round part on each side of the nose around the nostril, lower and to the side of the nose tip. It often appears in '콧방울이 벌렁거리다' (the nostrils flare) when someone is angry or out of breath. It also comes up in talk about makeup and skin care.

examples.en: I have a cold, so my voice sounds nasal.
That singer adds a nasal tone when singing.
The child acts cute in a nasal voice.

examples.ko: 콧소리 때문에 말이 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The nasal sound makes it hard to hear what you say.
My nose is blocked, so I end up talking through my nose.
Don't talk through your nose; speak clearly.

explain: 코가 막혔을 때 '콧소리가 나다'라고 해요. 일부러 코로 내는 귀여운 목소리는 '콧소리를 내다'라고 하는데, 애교를 부릴 때 많이 써요. 코가 막힌 목소리는 '코맹맹이 소리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: When your nose is blocked, you say '콧소리가 나다'. A cute voice made through the nose on purpose is '콧소리를 내다', often used when acting charming. A blocked-nose voice is also called '코맹맹이 소리'.

examples.en: I coat the injeolmi generously with bean powder.
I mix bean powder into milk and drink it.
Rice cake sprinkled with bean powder tastes nutty.
The bean powder blew around and got on my clothes.
You can use ground sesame instead of bean powder.
I bought a bag of bean powder at the mart.

explain: 볶은 콩을 갈아 만든 가루라서 인절미나 떡, 빙수에 고소한 맛을 더할 때 많이 써요. '밀가루'나 '쌀가루'처럼 '-가루'가 붙는 말 중 하나예요.

phrases.example: 저 집은 형제끼리 싸워서 완전 콩가루 집안이래요.
phrases.en: They say that family is a complete mess because the siblings fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족끼리 질서나 예의 없이 어지러운 집안을 속되게 말해요. 남의 집에 쓰면 실례라서 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slangy way to describe a family with no order or manners. It is rude to say about someone else's family.

explain_en: It is a powder made from ground roasted soybeans and is often used on injeolmi, rice cakes and shaved ice for a nutty flavor. It belongs to the '-가루' family with words like '밀가루' (wheat flour) and '쌀가루' (rice flour).

examples.en: I put soybean oil in the pan and fried an egg.
I made jeon with soybean oil.
Soybean oil is cheap, so we use a lot of it.
Using soybean oil for frying tastes clean.
We ran out of soybean oil, so I went to the mart.
You can use soybean oil instead of olive oil.

explain: 콩으로 짠 기름이에요. 보통 집에서는 '식용유'라고 부르는 경우가 많아요. 고소한 향이 나는 '참기름'이나 '들기름'과는 쓰임이 달라서 볶음, 전, 튀김처럼 일반 요리에 써요.
explain_en: It is oil pressed from soybeans. At home people often just call cooking oil '식용유'. It differs from the aromatic '참기름' (sesame oil) and '들기름' (perilla oil) and is used for general cooking like stir-frying, jeon and frying.

examples.en: My heart pounds before the presentation.
As the interview time got closer, my heart fluttered nervously.
It's our first date, so my heart is racing.

examples.ko: 콩닥콩닥 뛰는 소리가 들릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like you can hear my heart thumping.
I got startled and my heart started thumping.
My heart goes pitter-patter in front of the person I like.

explain: 작고 가볍게 빨리 뛰는 심장 소리를 나타내요. 설레거나 긴장될 때 많이 쓰고, 더 일반적인 말은 '두근두근'이에요. 심장이 아주 세게 뛸 때는 '쿵쾅쿵쾅'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a heart beating quickly in a small, light way, mostly when you are excited or nervous. The more general word is '두근두근'. For a much stronger heartbeat people say '쿵쾅쿵쾅'.

examples.ko: 저는 콩밥을 좋아해서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: I like rice with beans, so I often make it.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 콩밥이 싫어서 콩만 골라냈어요.
examples.en: As a child I hated bean rice and picked out only the beans.
Tonight's dinner is bean rice with doenjang stew.
They say rice with beans is good for your health.
I put beans in the rice and made bean rice.
Please give me one more bowl of bean rice.

explain: 쌀에 콩을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 비슷하게 '잡곡밥', '보리밥'처럼 재료를 앞에 붙여 말해요. 아래 표현처럼 말이 달라지는 쓰임도 있어요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 짓을 하면 콩밥을 먹게 돼요.
phrases.en: If you do bad things, you'll end up in prison.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감옥에 간다는 뜻의 속된 표현이에요. 가볍게 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slangy way to say someone goes to prison. It is used in a joking tone.

explain_en: It is rice cooked with beans mixed in. Similar words put the ingredient first, such as '잡곡밥' (multigrain rice) and '보리밥' (barley rice). It also has a figurative use shown below.

examples.en: I packed kongjaban in the lunch box.
Kongjaban is perfect as a side dish for rice.
Mom made the kongjaban sweet.
The kongjaban was too sweet, so I ate only a little.
Please give me one more plate of kongjaban.
There is some kongjaban left in the fridge.

explain: 콩을 간장에 달콤짭짤하게 졸인 밑반찬이에요. 검은콩으로 많이 만들어요. '자반'은 소금에 절인 생선(고등어 자반)에도 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a sweet and salty side dish of beans simmered in soy sauce, often made with black beans. The word '자반' is also used for salted fish, as in '고등어 자반'.

examples.en: Water is gushing out of the faucet.
It rained, so the stream is rushing along.
A pipe burst and water poured out.

examples.ko: 산속 샘에서 맑은 물이 콸콸 솟아요.
examples.en: Clear water gushes from the spring in the mountains.
Please don't leave the water running full blast.
I poured the water from the kettle into the cup in a rush.

explain: 많은 양의 물이 힘차게 쏟아지거나 흐르는 모습이에요. 적은 물이 가늘게 흐르면 '졸졸', 가늘게 계속 흐르면 '줄줄'이라고 해서 양과 세기가 달라요.
explain_en: It shows a large amount of water pouring or flowing forcefully. A thin small flow is '졸졸', and a thin continuous flow is '줄줄', so the amount and strength differ.

examples.en: The kids upstairs stomp around all day.
Please don't stomp; walk gently.
I woke up because of a banging sound at night.

examples.ko: 동생이 화가 나서 문을 쿵쾅거리며 나갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got angry and went out banging the doors.
There has been banging since morning because of construction, so it's noisy.
I was so nervous that my heart pounded.

explain: '쿵쿵'보다 크고 거친 소리가 여러 번 이어질 때 써요. 발소리, 문 닫는 소리, 공사 소리뿐 아니라 '가슴이 쿵쾅거리다'처럼 심장이 세게 뛸 때도 써요. 층간 소음 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when loud, rough thuds repeat, a bit stronger than '쿵쿵'. It fits footsteps, slamming doors and construction, and also a heart pounding hard as in '가슴이 쿵쾅거리다'. You often hear it in talk about noise from upstairs neighbors.

examples.en: There is a thumping sound from upstairs every night.
The child stomped around, and the downstairs neighbors complained.
Someone is banging on the door.
The elephant comes thudding along.
I'm so startled that my heart is thumping.

examples.ko: 쿵쿵 울리는 음악 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the music thumping.

explain: 무겁고 낮은 소리가 이어질 때 써요. 발소리, 문 두드리는 소리, 낮게 울리는 음악 소리, 심장 소리에도 써요. 소리가 더 시끄럽고 거칠면 '쿵쾅쿵쾅'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for heavy, low sounds that continue, such as footsteps, knocking, bass-heavy music and heartbeats. When the noise is louder and rougher, people say '쿵쾅쿵쾅'.

examples.en: A musty smell comes from the storage room.
The room has been closed for a long time, so it smells musty.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발장이 퀴퀴해서 환기했어요.
examples.en: The shoe cabinet smelled musty on the rainy day, so I aired it out.
The blanket smelled musty, so I washed it.
The basement smells stale, so let's open the window.

examples.ko: 옷장 안이 퀴퀴하지 않게 제습제를 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put a dehumidifier in the closet so it won't smell musty.

explain: 오래 닫혀 있거나 습한 곳의 곰팡내 같은 불쾌한 냄새에 써요. 주로 '퀴퀴한 냄새가 나다'라고 말해요. '쾨쾨하다'도 비슷한 말이에요. '꿉꿉하다'는 냄새보다 눅눅한 느낌을 말해서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It describes an unpleasant moldy smell from a closed or damp place, usually in '퀴퀴한 냄새가 나다'. '쾨쾨하다' is a similar word. '꿉꿉하다' is more about a damp, clammy feeling than a smell, so it differs a bit.

examples.en: Father came in clearing his throat loudly.
The teacher cleared his throat once.
I cleared my throat before entering the room.
Someone cleared their throat loudly, and everyone went quiet.

examples.ko: 그는 큰기침을 하고 나서 말을 시작했어요.
examples.en: He cleared his throat and then began to speak.

examples.ko: 어른이 큰기침을 하면 아이들이 눈치를 봐요.
examples.en: When an adult clears his throat loudly, the kids watch his mood.

explain: 병으로 하는 기침이 아니라 인기척을 내거나 점잖게 보이려고 일부러 크게 하는 기침이에요. '헛기침'도 비슷하게 신호로 하는 기침인데, 큰기침은 소리가 더 크고 위엄 있는 느낌이에요. 보통 '큰기침을 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: This is not a cough from illness but a loud one made on purpose to signal presence or to look dignified. '헛기침' is a similar signal cough, but '큰기침' is louder and feels more authoritative. It is usually used as '큰기침을 하다'.

examples.en: Write dialogue inside double quotation marks.
How are double and single quotation marks different?
We use double quotation marks for direct quotes.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 큰따옴표를 닫는 걸 잊었어요.
examples.en: I forgot to close the double quotation mark at the end of the sentence.
How do you type a double quotation mark on the keyboard?

examples.ko: 큰따옴표 안에 작은따옴표를 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can put single quotation marks inside double quotation marks.

explain: 사람의 말이나 글을 그대로 옮길 때 쓰는 "" 부호예요. 속으로 한 생각이나 강조할 때는 보통 작은따옴표 ''를 써요. 말할 때는 '쌍따옴표'라고도 해요.
explain_en: This is the "" mark used to reproduce someone's spoken or written words exactly. For inner thoughts or emphasis, the single quotation mark '' is usually used. In speech, people also say '쌍따옴표'.

examples.ko: 설날에 세배를 했어요? — 네, 가족들한테 큰절을 했어요.
examples.en: Did you do the New Year bow? — Yes, I bowed deeply to my family.

examples.ko: 설날 아침에 온 가족이 모여 할아버지께 큰절을 했어요.
examples.en: On New Year's morning the whole family gathered and bowed to grandfather.
At the wedding, the bride and groom bow deeply to their parents.

examples.ko: 신혼여행에서 돌아온 큰형과 형수는 집안 어른께 큰절을 했어요.
examples.en: My eldest brother and his wife, back from their honeymoon, bowed to the elders of the family.
I wore hanbok to bow to the elders.
The children learned how to do a deep bow.

explain: '큰절'은 무릎을 꿇고 이마가 손에 닿게 하는 격식 있는 절이에요. 설날의 '세배'는 새해에 어른께 드리는 큰절이고, 결혼식이나 제사 같은 큰 자리에서도 해요. 어른께는 '큰절을 드리다'라고 높여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '큰절' is a formal, full bow done kneeling with the forehead lowered toward the hands. '세배' on New Year's Day is a big bow given to elders, and it is also done at weddings and ancestral rites. To elders, people may say '큰절을 드리다' to be polite.

examples.en: I bought a nice big bag.
The apple is big, so even one makes me full.
If the writing is big, it's easy to read.
A child with big eyes is smiling.
The rooms in this house are spacious and bright.
I put in potatoes cut into big pieces.

explain: '크다'보다 보기 좋고 시원하게 큰 느낌이 있어요. '큼직하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 가방, 눈, 글씨, 채소 조각처럼 눈에 보이는 것에 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels more pleasantly and satisfyingly big than plain '크다'. It is used almost the same as '큼직하다'. It fits visible things such as bags, eyes, handwriting and chunks of vegetables.

examples.ko: 고기는 미리 건져 큼직큼직하게 썰어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I took the meat out beforehand and cut it into big pieces.

examples.ko: 감자를 큼직큼직 썰면 씹는 맛이 좋아요.
examples.en: If you cut potatoes into big pieces, they're nice to chew.
I cut the vegetables into big chunks and made curry.
I cut the tofu into big chunks and put it in the stew.

examples.ko: 사진 속 글자가 큼직큼직 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The letters in the photo are written big and bold.

examples.ko: 큼직큼직 썬 수박이 접시에 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: Watermelon cut into big pieces is on the plate.

explain: 음식이나 물건을 크게 자르거나 크게 쓴 모습에 써요. 반대로 작게 자를 때는 '잘게', 파 같은 것을 얇게 썰 때는 '송송'을 써요. 보통 '큼직큼직하게 썰다'처럼 '-하게'를 붙여서 말해요.
explain_en: It describes cutting or writing things in large pieces or sizes. For small pieces, people say '잘게', and for thinly sliced things like green onion, '송송'. It is usually said as '큼직큼직하게 썰다' with '-하게' added.

examples.en: The potatoes are in big chunks, so they're satisfying to eat.
I like soup with big chunks of ingredients.
I cut the meat into big pieces.
The pieces of meat at this restaurant are big.
The pieces are big, so they have a nice chew.
If the letters are big, you can see them from far away.

explain: 여러 개가 모두 크고 시원시원할 때 써요. 하나만 클 때는 '큼직하다'나 '큼지막하다'를 써요. 음식 재료나 글씨처럼 조각이나 글자가 여러 개 있는 것에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when several items are all big and bold. When only one thing is big, use '큼직하다' or '큼지막하다'. It suits things made of several pieces or letters, like food ingredients and handwriting.

examples.en: Someone behind me keeps giggling.
My friends giggled during class and got scolded.

examples.ko: 아이들이 이불 속에서 키득거리는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the kids giggling under the blanket.
I giggled to myself while reading a text.

examples.ko: 그 얘기만 들으면 나도 모르게 키득거리게 돼요.
examples.en: Whenever I hear that story, I giggle without meaning to.
Stop giggling and listen seriously.

explain: 웃음을 참으며 낮고 작게 웃는 모습이에요. '깔깔거리다'는 소리 내어 크게 웃는 느낌이라 다르고, '킥킥거리다'와는 비슷해요. 누군가 몰래 웃거나 놀리는 느낌으로 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes laughing low and softly while trying to hold the laughter in. '깔깔거리다' is a loud, open laugh, so it differs, while '킥킥거리다' is similar. It can also carry a sense of laughing secretly or teasingly.

examples.en: The kids sitting behind me are giggling.
The kids whisper and giggle under the blanket.
We giggled behind the teacher's back and got caught.
I turned at the sound of giggling and saw it was my friends.
My older sister, looking at her texts, is giggling to herself.

examples.ko: 장난이 재미있는지 동생이 키득키득 웃음을 참지 못해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling seems to find the prank funny and can't stop giggling.

explain: 웃음이 새어 나오는 작은 웃음소리를 계속 낼 때 써요. 한 번 짧게 웃으면 '킥'이라고 하고, '키득키득'은 여러 번 이어져요. 크게 웃는 '하하'나 '깔깔'과는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes small laughs that leak out one after another. A single short laugh is '킥', while '키득키득' keeps going. It feels different from big laughs like '하하' or '깔깔'.

examples.ko: 교실 여기저기서 킥킥 웃음을 참는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: Here and there in the classroom came the sound of people holding back giggles.
Someone behind me snickered.

examples.ko: 둘이 귓속말을 하며 킥킥 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering and giggling.
I tried to hold in my laughter, but giggles slipped out.
I giggle to myself while reading comics.
I heard a snicker and looked back.

explain: 웃음을 참다가 짧게 새어 나오는 소리예요. '키득키득'과 비슷한데 '킥킥'이 더 짧고 빠른 느낌이에요. 몰래 웃거나 놀리듯 웃을 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the short sound of laughter slipping out when you try to hold it in. It is similar to '키득키득', but '킥킥' feels shorter and quicker. It is often used for laughing secretly or teasingly.

examples.ko: 교실 여기저기서 킥킥거리며 웃음을 참는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: Here and there in the classroom people were snickering, holding back laughter.
My friend saw my mistake and is snickering.
What's so funny that you're giggling?
The two of them whispered and giggled.
You shouldn't giggle during class.
The giggling kids made the teacher laugh too.

explain: 웃음을 참으면서 낮게 웃는 모습이에요. 재미있어서 웃을 때도 쓰지만, 놀리듯이 웃을 때도 써요. '킥킥대다'라고도 하고, 뜻은 거의 같아요.
explain_en: It describes laughing low while trying to hold it in. It is used for laughing at something funny, but also for laughing in a teasing way. People also say '킥킥대다', with almost the same meaning.

examples.en: The drum is a typical percussion instrument.
I learned percussion when I was little.
The percussion sound in this piece is impressive.
In an orchestra, the percussion sits at the back.
Drums and gongs are also percussion instruments.
The percussionist came up on stage.

explain: 치거나 두드리거나 흔들어서 소리를 내는 악기를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 현악기, 관악기와 함께 악기를 나누는 큰 갈래예요. 꽹과리, 북, 장구 같은 전통 악기도 타악기예요.
explain_en: This groups instruments that make sound when struck, tapped or shaken. It is one of the main categories alongside string and wind instruments. Traditional instruments like the kkwaenggwari, buk and janggu are percussion too.

examples.en: This mirror is oval, so it looks pretty.
An egg is close to an oval shape.
I put the salad on an oval plate.
Planets travel along elliptical orbits.
Glasses suit me because my face is oval.

examples.ko: 타원형 테이블은 방에 들어가기엔 너무 커요.
examples.en: The oval table is too big to fit in the room.

explain: 동그란 '원형'을 옆으로 길게 늘인 모양을 말해요. 달걀 모양은 '계란형'이라고도 하는데, 얼굴이나 모양을 말할 때 많이 써요. '타원'만 쓰기도 하지만 모양을 말할 때는 '타원형'이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This is a shape like a round circle (원형) stretched lengthwise. An egg-like shape is also called '계란형', often for faces. You can say just '타원', but '타원형' sounds natural when describing a shape.

examples.en: At graduation we buried a time capsule in the ground.

examples.ko: 십 년 뒤에 타임캡슐을 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to open the time capsule ten years later.
I put letters and photos in the time capsule.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 타임캡슐에 무엇을 넣을지 정했어요.
examples.en: Our class decided what to put in the time capsule.
I forgot where the time capsule is buried.

examples.ko: 이 앨범은 타임캡슐처럼 옛날 모습을 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This album holds old memories like a time capsule.

explain: 먼 훗날 열어 보려고 물건을 넣어 묻어 두는 통을 말해요. '묻다', '열다', '넣다'와 같이 자주 쓰여요. 학교나 모임에서 기념으로 하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: This is a container filled with items and buried to be opened in the distant future. It often goes with '묻다' (bury), '열다' (open) and '넣다' (put in). Schools and groups often make one as a keepsake.

examples.en: I practiced with a friend at the table tennis table.

examples.ko: 학교 체육관에 탁구대가 네 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are four table tennis tables in the school gym.
I folded the table tennis table and stood it against the wall.
I'm looking into buying a new table tennis table.
The ball fell on the table tennis table.
Shall we play a game at our table?

explain: 탁구를 치는 '대(판)'를 말하고, 탁구를 하는 장소는 '탁구장'이라고 해서 구별해요. 보통 '탁구를 치다'라고 말해요. 가운데 있는 그물은 '네트'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the table itself, while the place for playing is called '탁구장', so keep them apart. People normally say '탁구를 치다'. The net in the middle is called '네트'.

examples.en: I put a table clock on my desk.
I woke up to the table clock's alarm.
I got a table clock as a birthday present.
The table clock is five minutes slow.
After I changed the battery, the table clock works again.
A quiet table clock is good for a bedroom.

explain: 책상이나 탁자 위에 놓고 쓰는 작은 시계예요. 벽에 거는 '벽시계', 손목에 차는 '손목시계'와 짝으로 기억해 두세요. 알람이 있으면 '알람시계'나 '자명종'이라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a small clock placed on a desk or table. Remember it alongside '벽시계' (wall clock) and '손목시계' (wristwatch). With an alarm it may also be called '알람시계' or '자명종'.

examples.en: Dual-income couples leave their children at a daycare center.
A daycare center opened inside the company.
Teachers look after the children at the daycare center.
It's convenient because there's a daycare center near my house.
How much does the daycare center cost?
I drop my child at the daycare center and go to work.

explain: 부모가 일하는 동안 어린아이를 맡아 돌보는 곳이에요. 요즘은 '어린이집'이라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 탁아소는 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 아이를 맡길 때는 '맡기다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a place that cares for young children while parents work. These days '어린이집' is used more, and '탁아소' sounds a bit old-fashioned. To leave a child there, use '맡기다'.

examples.en: The amusement park has many kinds of rides.
Children like toy vehicles.
Buses, subways and taxis are all vehicles.
On this island there's nothing to ride but bicycles.
Which ride was the most fun?

examples.ko: 탈것을 이용할 때는 안전이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: Safety matters most when you use any vehicle.

explain: 버스, 기차, 자전거처럼 사람이 타는 것을 두루 말해요. 뉴스나 설명문에서는 '교통수단'을 많이 쓰고, '탈것'은 아이들 이야기나 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요. 놀이공원에서 타는 것은 '놀이기구'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It covers anything people ride, such as buses, trains and bicycles. News and explanatory texts prefer '교통수단', while '탈것' is more casual, often used in talk about children. Amusement park rides are also called '놀이기구'.

examples.en: I developed hair loss because of stress.
If you have hair loss, try consulting a doctor.
My father also suffered from hair loss.
I'm looking for a shampoo that's good for hair loss.
The sooner you start treating hair loss, the better.
These days even young people worry about hair loss.

explain: '탈모'는 머리카락이 빠지는 일을 두루 말하고, '탈모증'은 그것이 병처럼 계속될 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '탈모'라고 하거나 '머리가 빠지다'라고 많이 해요. 병원이나 광고에서는 '탈모증'을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: '탈모' refers to hair falling out in general, while '탈모증' is used when it continues like a medical condition. In daily talk people often just say '탈모' or '머리가 빠지다'. You often see '탈모증' at hospitals and in ads.

examples.ko: 불이 나면 탈출구로 빨리 나가야 해요.
examples.en: If there's a fire, you must get out quickly through the exit.
At the theater I first checked where the exit was.

examples.ko: 요즘 너무 힘들어서 어디론가 탈출구를 찾고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm so worn out these days that I want to find a way out somewhere.
The exit was blocked, and people panicked.

examples.ko: 이 게임에서는 탈출구를 찾는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: The goal in this game is to find the way out.
Every building has exit signs.

explain: 위험하거나 갇힌 곳에서 빠져나가는 길이에요. 건물의 초록색 표지는 보통 '비상구'라고 부르고, '탈출구'는 더 넓게 쓰여요. 힘든 상황에서 벗어날 방법을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is the way out of a dangerous or trapped place. The green sign in buildings is usually called '비상구', while '탈출구' is used more broadly. It can also mean a way to escape a hard situation.

examples.en: I sprayed deodorizer in the shoe cabinet.
I replaced the fridge deodorizer with a new one.
Even when I spray deodorizer, the smell doesn't go away.
I left a deodorizer in the car.
I like this deodorizer because it has no scent.
I sprayed the clothes with deodorizer and let them dry.

explain: 냄새를 없애는 물건이에요. 좋은 향으로 덮는 '방향제'와 달라요. 몸에 바르는 것은 보통 '데오도란트'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is a product that removes odors. It differs from '방향제' (air freshener), which covers smells with a pleasant scent. The kind applied to the body is usually called '데오도란트'.

examples.ko: 사은품이 탐나서 필요 없는 책을 두 권이나 샀어요.
examples.en: I wanted the free gift so much that I bought two books I didn't need.
I really covet that bag.
If there's something I want, I wait until payday.

examples.ko: 친구 신발이 탐났지만 말은 못 했어요.
examples.en: I coveted my friend's shoes but couldn't say so.
What do you want that badly?

examples.ko: 탐나더라도 남의 물건은 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you want it, you must not take other people's things.

explain: '갖고 싶다'보다 욕심이 나서 마음이 끌린다는 느낌이에요. 갖고 싶은 것에 '이/가'를 붙여서 '가방이 탐나요'라고 해요. '탐내다'는 '가방을 탐내요'처럼 '을/를'과 쓰는 다른 동사예요. '욕심나다'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '갖고 싶다', a greedy pull toward something. The thing wanted takes '이/가', as in '가방이 탐나요'. '탐내다' is a different verb used with '을/를', as in '가방을 탐내요'. '욕심나다' is used similarly.

examples.en: After a baby is born, the umbilical cord is cut.
The mother and baby are connected by the umbilical cord.
The father cut the umbilical cord himself.
The place where the umbilical cord falls off becomes the belly button.
The cord was wrapped around the neck, so we were worried.
The umbilical cord delivers nutrition to the baby.

explain: 엄마 배 속에서 아기가 영양을 받는 줄이에요. 태어난 뒤에 자르고 남은 자리가 '배꼽'이에요. 의학에서는 '제대'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '탯줄'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the cord through which a baby receives nourishment in the womb. After birth it is cut, and the place left behind is the '배꼽' (belly button). Medicine also uses '제대', but daily speech says '탯줄'.

examples.ko: 저는 턱걸이를 열 개 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do ten chin-ups.
I did chin-ups on the bar in the park.
Chin-ups are good exercise for the arms and back.

examples.ko: 턱걸이가 너무 어려워서 한 개도 못 해요.
examples.en: Chin-ups are so hard that I can't do even one.
I'm practicing chin-ups a little every day.
My shoulder hurt while I was doing chin-ups.

explain: 철봉을 잡고 몸을 끌어올려 턱이 철봉 위로 오게 하는 운동이에요. 바닥에서 하는 '팔굽혀펴기'와 구별해요. 보통 '턱걸이를 하다'라고 말해요. 아래처럼 겨우 해냈다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: My score was borderline, but I just barely passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준에 겨우 맞춰 간신히 통과한다는 뜻이에요. 시험, 입학, 심사 같은 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means just barely meeting the cutoff. Used for exams, admissions and screenings.

explain_en: It is the exercise of pulling yourself up on a bar until your chin is over it. Do not mix it up with '팔굽혀펴기' (push-ups), done on the floor. It is normally said as '턱걸이를 하다'. It is also used to mean barely managing something, as shown below.
